original_card.question: Can a template or call contract leave two or more unpaid coordinates per live family?
methods: State a replacement for the coverage identity (mass = 72W + 64N) and the contract change that realizes it, with its implementation cost.
Find an obstruction: show which data-endpoint obligation forces exactly one unpaid coordinate in the current template.
original_card.acceptance_gate: An explicit replacement identity, verified on a small complete instance with dirty inputs, priced with ceiling.ceiling(unpaid=...). A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Explain where the single unpaid coordinate per family comes from in the hosted template; propose one change and price it. Ideal budget: two unpaid coordinates per family is 3.77x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: The deficit is one coordinate per family minus the centre charge; doubling unpaid coordinates per family scales it directly.
allowed_variations: One template change or one endpoint-contract change.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Counting a coordinate as unpaid while leaving it unadvanced in the data endpoint.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: On the selected #4470 p16 Laurent controller, can the ring substitution Q -> Qa*Qb (a second central Gaussian line on a fresh axis) leave two unpaid coordinates per main family at a fully charged cost that beats the selected fixed-invoice root?
scope_change_reason: The card's starting points price the obsolete #1094 hosted template (mass = 72W + 64N, ceiling.ceiling(unpaid=...)). The selected record is now the #4470 productive-helper interface, where that identity and ceiling do not apply. This package rebinds the card to the selected invoice: it identifies the single unpaid coordinate as the central line Q = C_q in every main target, names one changed call contract (Q -> Qa*Qb), and derives a replacement bound for it instead of reusing the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
bottleneck_link: In the selected invoice the 3,584 main targets each carry one central coordinate that no paid idle advances. A second central coordinate per family is worth 3.39x the selected root under the optimistic relaxation. That is the card's lever on the current interface, so its price decides whether the coverage lever is live.
stop_rule: Stop after the source identity, the formal and literal instance, the credit-rank lemma, the optimistic root, the native allowance, the full-credit obstruction and the partial-credit ceiling are certified. Do not search for a redesigned ten-axis native word in this package.
evidence: Exact identity on the pinned #4470 invoice: every main target is 1 + 8k with an 8k paid idle (or 1 + 8*18 for the long target); the rank-one surplus is 752 = 18*(H1 - P1 + V + 2VB) - V. The substitution Q -> Qa*Qb is an exact controller with two central exponents per target, checked formally and on six dirty F2^3 inputs. Optimistic relaxation (natives unchanged, thin shears rank 2): root in (0.01023582, 0.010235821), 3.39x. Credit-rank lemma: c credited targets need c q_b-touching paid requests, so the natives need at least 1,904. Allowance: at most 1,859 extra rank-one units keep a positive surplus at the selected root. Conjugation-charged profile: rank-one surplus -1,376. Full-credit theorem: any incremental realization (selected paid profile kept, q_b added to requests or new requests) is strictly below the selected surplus at every 0 < C < 1. Partial-credit incremental realizations cannot certify C = 0.003035069 (+0.49% ceiling).
